cards.explanation: The answer is Rejected them. David's first words are, "You have rejected us, O God; You have broken us; You have been angry; restore us!" (Psalm 60:1) He doesn't dress it up one bit, friends. He says it straight to God and asks for restoring in the same breath.

The answer is True. David says it plainly: "You have shaken the land and torn it open." (Psalm 60:2) That's a whole lot of shaking, friends. And he keeps talking to God the whole time instead of backing out of the room.
The answer is quaking, friends. David says, "Heal its fractures, for it is quaking." (Psalm 60:2) The land is shaking, and he takes that shaking straight to God. He doesn't keep it to himself.

The answer is False. There are no easy days in this verse. David says, "You have shown Your people hardship; we are staggered from the wine You made us drink." (Psalm 60:3) He puts the hardship on the table, friends, and he doesn't hide it.

The answer is So they can flee the bow. God has raised a banner for those who fear Him, "…that they may flee the bow." (Psalm 60:4) The banner is for those who fear Him, friends. The reason given is fleeing the bow.

The answer is beloved, friends. David asks God to "Respond and save us with Your right hand, that Your beloved may be delivered." (Psalm 60:5) He calls them God's beloved right there in the prayer. That's who he wants delivered.

The answer is He says He will triumph. God has spoken from His sanctuary: "I will triumph!" (Psalm 60:6) And what an opening, friends. After all that rejection and hardship in David's prayer, those are the first words out of God's mouth.
The answer is True. God says, "Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine…" (Psalm 60:7) Both are on the list, friends. When God names a place and says it's His, that settles it.

The answer is Things God wears and holds. God says, "Ephraim is My helmet, Judah is My scepter." (Psalm 60:7) A helmet is worn and a scepter is held, friends. Both are pictures of something close to Him.
The answer is False. God says, "over Philistia I shout in triumph." (Psalm 60:8) It's a shout of triumph, friends. There's no crying of sorrow in it.
The answer is fortified, friends. David asks, "Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?" (Psalm 60:9) A fortified city has defenses built around it. So it's no easy walk in.
The answer is March out with them. David asks, "Will You no longer march out, O God, with our armies?" (Psalm 60:10) He wants God going out with them, friends, not staying behind.
The answer is man, friends. David says, "Give us aid against the enemy, for the help of man is worthless." (Psalm 60:11) He says it plainly. Nobody has to wonder why he's asking God.

The answer is True. It's the last line, friends: "With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies." (Psalm 60:12) David ends the song with God at the center. Those are the very last words.
